subject: safe way to inspect a ggplot object?

messages.author: fe0b9140b8bdf3c1
messages.subject: safe way to inspect a ggplot object?
parts:
Hi -

I've got a ggplot2 plot object, named p, which I'm passing around in
my programs.

I'd like to programmatically inspect this object for it's current
aspect ratio (if one it set), and make adjustments accordingly.

Currently, I'm doing this with this call:

ratio <- p$options$aspect

Is there a better, safe way to inspect a ggplot2 object?

Code snippet below:

library(ggplot2)
library(maps)
df <- map_data("county","california")
p <- qplot(long,lat,data=df, group=group, geom="polygon")

Thanks!

MD

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: safe way to inspect a ggplot object?
parts:
Hi,

maybe you could define your own accessor function, a bit like for S4
slots, and create a basic test to see immediately if the
implementation is broken in a future release of ggplot2,

library(ggplot2)
getAspect = function(p)
p$options$aspect

library(testthat)

context("Basic tests")
test_that("retrieving a plot aspect ratio works", {
expect_that(is.null(getAspect(qplot(1,1))), is_true())
expect_that(getAspect(qplot(1,1, asp=2)), equals(2))
})

Best,

baptiste

isolate where things have to be fixed. I *think* Michael is asking if
the structure is intended to be used in the same way the package's
functions are used and with the same expectation of stability. If not,
maybe a suite of accessor functions in the package would be useful.

> is intended to be used in the same way the package's functions are used and
> with the same expectation of stability.  If not, maybe a suite of accessor

Currently, if you want to modify the options manually you're on your
own. The structure is likely to remain the same in the future, but I
don't want to make any guarantees. From my perspective even making an
options accessor function is not likely to help much, because if I do
change things I might even change the underlying data structure which
will break code anyway.

messages.author: 4e69b94a09c8cf3b
messages.subject: Re: safe way to inspect a ggplot object?
parts:
In that case, I think you may want to use

p$options$aspect.ratio


The likely scenario for change that the existing structure is extended.
Using partial name match would likely lead to "unpredictable results".
Say nothing else is touched but the structure is extended to add

p$options$aspect.multiplier

as another attribute. Trouble for your test for sure.


(For later users that may not catch Michael's tongue-in-cheek, make sure
you read through the entire thread to find out what Hadley actually wrote.)
